import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd
import io

# For a meaningful visualization, it's better to use a more complete dataset.
# We'll use seaborn's built-in Titanic dataset which matches the user's data structure.
df = sns.load_dataset('titanic')

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", palette="viridis")

# Create a figure and a set of subplots with a specific layout
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(18, 14), constrained_layout=True)
gs = fig.add_gridspec(3, 2)

# Add a main title
fig.suptitle('Comprehensive Analysis of Titanic Survival Factors', fontsize=24, weight='bold')

# --- Plot 1: Survival Rate by Passenger Class (Top Left) ---
ax1 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 0])
sns.countplot(data=df, x='class', hue='alive', ax=ax1, order=['First', 'Second', 'Third'])
ax1.set_title('Survival Counts by Passenger Class', fontsize=16, weight='bold')
ax1.set_xlabel('Passenger Class', fontsize=12)
ax1.set_ylabel('Number of Passengers', fontsize=12)
ax1.legend(title='Status')

# --- Plot 2: Survival Rate by Sex (Top Right) ---
ax2 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 1])
sns.countplot(data=df, x='sex', hue='alive', ax=ax2)
ax2.set_title('Survival Counts by Sex', fontsize=16, weight='bold')
ax2.set_xlabel('Sex', fontsize=12)
ax2.set_ylabel('Number of Passengers', fontsize=12)
ax2.legend(title='Status')

# --- Plot 3: Age Distribution by Survival Status (Middle Row, Spanning both columns) ---
ax3 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, :])
sns.kdeplot(data=df, x='age', hue='alive', fill=True, common_norm=False, ax=ax3, alpha=0.5, linewidth=2)
ax3.set_title('Age Distribution of Survivors vs. Non-Survivors', fontsize=16, weight='bold')
ax3.set_xlabel('Age', fontsize=12)
ax3.set_ylabel('Density', fontsize=12)
ax3.legend(title='Status', labels=['Survived', 'Did not survive'])

# --- Plot 4: Violin plot of Age and Fare by Class and Survival (Bottom Left) ---
ax4 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 0])
sns.violinplot(data=df, x='class', y='age', hue='alive', split=True, ax=ax4, inner='quart', palette='muted')
ax4.set_title('Age Distribution by Class and Survival', fontsize=16, weight='bold')
ax4.set_xlabel('Passenger Class', fontsize=12)
ax4.set_ylabel('Age', fontsize=12)
ax4.legend(title='Status')

# --- Plot 5: Fare Distribution by Embark Town and Survival (Bottom Right) ---
ax5 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 1])
sns.stripplot(data=df, x='embark_town', y='fare', hue='alive', dodge=True, alpha=0.7, jitter=0.3, ax=ax5, order=['Southampton', 'Cherbourg', 'Queenstown'])
ax5.set_title('Fare Distribution by Embark Town and Survival', fontsize=16, weight='bold')
ax5.set_xlabel('Port of Embarkation', fontsize=12)
ax5.set_ylabel('Fare (log scale)', fontsize=12)
ax5.set_yscale('log') # Fare is highly skewed, log scale helps visualization
ax5.legend(title='Status')

# Save the figure with high resolution
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
